_why: ONE COMPLETION PREDICATE, TWO RUNTIMES. The core decides whether a journey
dashboard decides whether to redirect an operator into onboarding
They answer the same question and they are written in different languages,
so nothing but a shared table can stop them drifting — and a drift here is
not cosmetic: one side would announce 'Your Cabinet is ready' while the
other bounced the operator back into the wizard.
Each case below is asserted by BOTH suites:
A case added here with no matching behaviour turns one of them red.
THE STATES ARE PARTIAL ON PURPOSE. Both predicates read exactly two fields;
a case carrying a whole journey would test the fixture builder rather than
the predicate, and would hide which field decided the answer.

cases.name: empty
cases.why: no journey at all — onboarding has not run

cases.name: welcome
cases.why: the three questions are open; nothing has been granted or read

cases.name: charter_pending
cases.why: the Charter is proposed and NOT approved — no byte has been read

cases.name: ratified_without_dividend
cases.why: both halves are required: a grant with nothing delivered is not an arrival

cases.name: dividend_without_charter
cases.why: a result with no approved grant behind it is the one shape that must never read as done

cases.name: dividend_ready
cases.why: the promise is kept the moment the read happens under the approved Charter

cases.name: complete
cases.why: the terminal stage, with the facts behind it

cases.name: complete_stage_without_the_facts
cases.why: THE FALSE ARRIVAL. A stage value alone can be hand-edited, half-restored or written by a buggy build; it must never be enough to announce a success the product cannot show.

cases.name: orientation_offered
cases.why: the legacy terminal stage — the Captain's own live journey — reads as arrived without its stored state being rewritten

cases.name: revoked_after_arriving
cases.why: TAKING ACCESS BACK DOES NOT UN-DELIVER THE RESULT. Revoke stops future reads; it does not erase the Charter that was approved or the result that was given, so this journey stays finished and the operator is not shoved back into the wizard for exercising a control. What stops the arrival SCREEN here is the card kind (revoked), not this predicate.

cases.name: purged
cases.why: what _fresh_state(stage='purged') writes — the record is gone
